title: A Forgotten Particle May Explain Why the Universe Exists
summary:
Scientists have a new idea about why the universe exists at all. Long ago, matter and antimatter were made in almost equal amounts. When they meet, they destroy each other. If the amounts had been exactly equal, almost nothing would be left. There would be no stars, planets, or life.

Researchers from the University of Southampton and the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur say a forgotten particle may have helped. It is a heavier cousin of the neutrino, a tiny particle that rarely touches normal matter. Scientists long thought it was too weakly connected to matter to count.

But the researchers found that it breaks down very slowly. So it lived long enough to briefly rule the young universe's energy as the universe cooled after the Big Bang. That may have changed the temperature when tiny particles met their opposites, with help from the Higgs boson. That temperature worked like a switch, shaping how a little extra matter survived.

Study author Dr. Rishav Roshan said, "The fact that we are here at all proves that an asymmetry between matter and antimatter occurred." The idea was published in Physical Review Letters. It is a new idea, not proof.
why_it_matters: Asking why anything exists at all is one of the biggest questions you can wonder about.
